assumptions: Took the issue's recommended fix shape rather than the alternative: kept the engine's `DesignPipelineInput.noFreshen` / `noFill` contract exactly as-is (design-pipeline/index.ts:55 and :90 still skip a phase only on `=== true`) and corrected only the command layer's option read. The defect is at the command boundary; the engine contract is coherent and is consumed by tests and callers beyond this command.

Used `opts.freshen === false` / `opts.fill === false` rather than a truthiness check (`!opts.freshen`). Empirically verified against the exact commander in use (12.1.0): Commander ALWAYS populates `freshen`/`fill`, defaulting both to `true`, so only an explicit `false` distinguishes 'flag passed' from 'flag absent'. A `=== undefined` test would never fire. This also preserves the command's established contract of OMITTING unsupplied flags from the input rather than sending `false` for them.

Also corrected the `DesignPipelineCliOptions` interface (`noFreshen?`/`noFill?` -> `freshen?`/`fill?`). This is part of the same root cause, not scope creep: the interface asserted a shape Commander never produces, which is precisely why the inert reads typechecked cleanly and the bug survived review. Leaving it would let the same defect be reintroduced silently.

INVERTED AN EXISTING PASSING TEST. The block at packages/cli/tests/commands/design-pipeline-command.test.ts:140-172 was a deliberate CHARACTERIZATION block that pinned the BROKEN behavior (asserting the input does NOT contain `noFreshen`/`noFill`). Those three assertions now assert the opposite. This is intended: the original block's own comment stated 'These tests will go red the moment it lands, which is exactly the signal wanted.' A reviewer must see that a previously-passing assertion changed meaning.

Added two guard tests beyond a straight inversion, covering the over-correction: a bare run must still OMIT both keys, and `--no-freshen` alone must not set `noFill`. Without these, a fix keyed off key-presence rather than `=== false` would pass the inverted assertions while skipping every phase on every run. Both guards pass in the pre-fix and post-fix states by design; they constrain the fix, they do not reproduce the bug.

Held scope to design-pipeline.ts only. Three sibling instances of the identical defect class were found and deliberately NOT touched: test-craft.ts:86 (issue #1882, separate lane in flight), dashboard.ts:121, and fleet/budget-check.ts:170 (both untracked and outside the confirmed batch, reported separately by the fleet). Note budget-check.ts:219 already uses the correct `opts.refresh === false` form in the same file as its broken :170 read.
rootCause: Commander's negated-flag convention applied backwards. `.option('--no-freshen')` defines an option named `freshen` (default `true`, set to `false` when passed) and never produces a `noFreshen` key. The action read `opts.noFreshen === true` / `opts.noFill === true`, which are `undefined` on every code path, so `input.noFreshen` / `input.noFill` were never set and the engine always ran FRESHEN and FILL. Two documented flags were silently inert, failing in the worst direction: FILL is the expensive phase the flag exists to avoid.
